label: F-a5e029

findings.note: TheAgyQuotaReportPicksTheResetTests.cs:28-40 edits a JsonNode that `JsonNode.Parse` has just made as a local copy and returns a new string. No shared or input value is mutated, so the immutability rule is not broken in any meaningful way.

The plan's cancellation rule (D5, S42) and the docstring at QuotaCooldowns.cs:168 say only that a cancelled PROBE parks nothing. A refusal with a stated reset that finished before a cancel is a real fact, and parking it from the completed results is what D5 intends.

The plan's gate table explicitly rejected this (F0: 'the 16 KiB budget is not enforced when unknown model keys accumulate'). Expired entries drop at the next write (QuotaCooldowns.cs:279), and a cap with eviction could un-park a spent row.

DecidedAsync (QuotaCooldowns.cs:199-205) does await each key's probe in turn. But only agy keys probe, D3's table holds a handful of agy keys, each is bounded at 30 s as the plan says (§8), and the scenario of 10 keys all timing out is unrealistic.
D4 says 'read on every CanRun, no cache (it is under 16 KiB for ever)'. PanelService.cs:422 reading through Standing on each call is the plan's decided design.
AgyError.cs:40 rejoins the rest of stderr only for lines that start with AGY_ERROR, so the cost is markers × length, not O(N²) per line. With stderr of a few lines this is a small cleanup, not Major.

AgyQuotaReport.cs:58 is lazy LINQ, so the same text is parsed a second time only after the whole-text parse has failed, and the result is unchanged. Walking back to the last JSON line is what the plan's own docstring describes.
This asks for the mtime or in-memory cache that D4 explicitly decided against ('no cache'). It duplicates index 4.

The title's crash does not exist: `Max` runs only when `known.Count > 0` (AgyQuotaReport.cs:121-129). The null Adapter it lands on cannot happen either, because DecidedAsync groups by `Adapter?.QuotaKeyOf(...) ?? ""` and drops empty keys (QuotaCooldowns.cs:198), so every refusal that reaches line 246 has an adapter.

A trailing `\r` after `AGY_ERROR: {` does not stop the body from starting with `{` (AgyError.cs:47), and JSON treats `\r` as whitespace, so `ParseValue` and `JsonDocument.Parse` still succeed. The only layout that fails, a marker alone on its line, fails the same way with LF.

System.Text.Json round-trips DateTimeOffset at full tick precision. Unchanged entries in `next` come straight from the `current` that was read from the file, so SequenceEqual (QuotaCooldowns.cs:280) is not fooled, and the DirectoryNotFound framing of the title is never shown to be a problem.
The plan requires the refusal notice to name its cause, the lock (D4, S37). This is a local tool whose notice goes to the owner of the data directory, so naming the path discloses nothing sensitive.
It duplicates indexes 4 and 7, and D4 decided 'read on every decision, no cache' on purpose so that other coai-mcp processes see a park on their next round (§8).
It duplicates index 5: AgyError.cs:40 rejoins the remaining lines once per marker line, which is wasteful but negligible for agy's short stderr.

The plan (§8) says the lock is released with its handle and 'nothing stale is left to sweep', so remediation advice about a wedged lock would be wrong. The notice at QuotaCooldowns.cs:255 already says what was lost, as S37 requires.

summary: Most findings either ask for things the plan explicitly decided against (no cache, no 16 KiB cap with eviction, a notice that names the lock) or misread the code (the null-Adapter 'blocking' finding, CRLF, DateTimeOffset precision). What is left is minor: the serial agy probes and the repeated stderr joins, the latter reported twice, so a team would gain very little from acting on this review.
